opening_message:
Ticket 1: Robert Weber (employee ID E047) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E047.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Robert Weber (E047) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, max is write since Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, not Payroll Specialist. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB check: Robert Weber (E047) is a contractor with basic security training (note: this conflicts with the earlier note listing full-time). Contractors max is read (or write only with advanced training); never admin. Requested admin for Source Code exceeds max, so grant read.
reason: Robert Weber (E047) requested admin access to Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role; E047's role is Payroll Specialist, so admin is not justified even under the full-time interpretation (max would be write). The Security agent's database check lists E047 as a contractor with basic security training, which yields a maximum of read (write requires advanced training; admin is never allowed for contractors). Because the requested level (admin) exceeds the allowable maximum, grant the maximum of read. Granting read is also safe under the conflicting full-time record.

- Security agent: role Payroll Specialist (not looked up), employment type contractor (looked up), security training basic (looked up), recommendation read.

Conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor. Security looked up employment type in own database; HR also looked up in own database. So there's conflicting information.

Policy:
- full_time: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Source Code owned by Engineer role. Payroll Specialist doesn't own, so max write.
- contractor: read, or write if advanced training. Never admin. Security says basic training, so max read.

Requested: admin.

Either way, admin is above max. So grant the maximum. The max depends on employment type: if full_time, max write; if contractor with basic training, max read.

Given the direct conflict, I need to make a judgment call. The Security agent explicitly noted the discrepancy and their DB lookup result (contractor, basic training). I'll trust the Security agent's more directly verified info? But HR also verified.
